title: The persistent post-drought runoff deficit belonged to southern Australia after 1997, not to drought length or rain deficit: one annual method on 561 Australian and 670 US catchments, 1951-2025
abstract: Question: why do multi-year droughts leave a persistent runoff deficit in south-east Australia but not in the contiguous US? Approach: we applied one annual method, with the same code and rules, to all 561 CAMELS-AUS v2.03 catchments (1951-2021) and 670 CAMELS-US catchments (1951-2025). The model is sqrt(runoff) linear in rain, previous-year rain and temperature, fitted on years outside droughts. For each catchment, R10 is the mean standardised residual in the 10 years after its most severe drought. We used cluster-bootstrap intervals over 2-degree cells, common time-shift placebos, nearest-neighbour matching and transfer tests. Results: R10 was -0.58 SD (95% CI -0.79 to -0.36) in southern Australia, +0.23 in northern Australia and +0.03 (-0.05 to +0.10) in the US. Drought dose did not explain the contrast. US droughts of 7 years or more had R10 of +0.17 to +0.27. In southern Australia after 1997, short and long droughts gave -0.78 and -0.72, and the slope on cumulative rain deficit was -0.02 (-0.72 to +0.66). Southern catchments with a 5% Millennium Drought rain deficit had the same 2010-2021 deficit as those with a 20% deficit. Catchment properties removed about one third of the continental gap. Matched US catchments had -0.01 against -0.73. Dry catchments (runoff ratio below 0.1) had -1.16 in southern Australia after 1997 but +0.24 there before 1997, +0.17 in northern Australia and -0.04 in the US. Wet years did not reduce the deficit. The data agree better with a regional southern Australian change that started with the Millennium Drought than with a drought-length effect. Limitations: one regional episode, so era and drought are not separable; annual rain-temperature model; different data sources on the two continents; several post hoc analyses.

display.caption: Runoff residual relative to the 1951-1996 relation. Southern Australian catchments, split by their own 1997-2009 rain deficit, fall together from 1997 and stay low; northern Australia and the US do not.
R10 by runoff-ratio class: dry catchments lose runoff only in southern Australia after 1997 (95% cluster-bootstrap intervals; post hoc).
Pooled regressions, matching and transfer tests: drought dose does not reduce the AU-US gap; catchment properties remove about one third; an indicator for southern Australia after 1997 holds the gap.
